            and any(f"conv_{c.lower()}" in h["name"] for c in conventions)]


def check(task, workspace: Path, file: str, revert, conventions: set[str]) -> dict:
    """Run the task's tests on the workspace and on a copy with `revert` applied to `file`."""
    from ..verify import verify
    after = verify(workspace, task)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        rev = Path(tmp) / "ws"
        shutil.copytree(workspace, rev)
        target = rev / file
        target.write_text(apply(target.read_text(), revert))
        before = verify(rev, task)
    collected = bool(before["hidden"]) and not any("collect" in (h.get("name") or "") for h in before["hidden"])
    failing = conv_failures(before, conventions)
    status = ("invalid: tests fail with the change" if not after["passed"] else
              "inconclusive: reverted workspace does not run" if not collected else
              "validated" if failing else "not validated: the tests do not depend on the change")
    return {"status": status, "validated": status == "validated", "after_passed": after["passed"],
            "reverted_conv_failures": failing,
            "reverted_other_failures": [h["name"] for h in before["hidden"] if not h["passed"] and h["name"] not in failing]}


def auto_revert(source: str, applied: str, named_params: set[str] | None = None) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """Derive the counterfactual edit for the statement the note's applied line belongs to.

    simple statement (assignment, call, raise, return, ...)  remove it (`pass` keeps the block valid)
    `if` header whose body rejects (raise / return)          remove the whole check: the claim is "reject when"
    `if` header whose body acts                              keep the body, drop the condition: the claim is
                                                             "do this only when"
    Returns (old_text, new_text) to apply to the file, or None when no statement can be found."""
    import ast
    import textwrap
    lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    target = " ".join(applied.split())
    idx = next((i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if target and target in " ".join(ln.split())), None)
    if idx is None:
        return None
    tree = ast.parse(source)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):  # D60: a rule carried by a signature: ignore the parameter the note names
        if isinstance(fn, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and fn.lineno - 1 == idx and named_params:
            params = [a.arg for a in fn.args.args + fn.args.kwonlyargs if a.arg in named_params]
            if params:
                first = fn.body[0]
                if isinstance(first, ast.Expr) and isinstance(getattr(first, "value", None), ast.Constant) and isinstance(first.value.value, str) and len(fn.body) > 1:
                    first = fn.body[1]  # keep the docstring first
                body_line = lines[first.lineno - 1]
                ind = body_line[: len(body_line) - len(body_line.lstrip())]
                return body_line, "".join(f"{ind}{p} = None  # counterfactual: the parameter is ignored\n" for p in params) + body_line
    best = None
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.stmt) and not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) \
                and node.lineno - 1 <= idx <= node.end_lineno - 1:
            if best is None or (node.end_lineno - node.lineno) < (best.end_lineno - best.lineno):
                best = node
    if best is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(best, ast.If) and best.lineno - 1 == idx and not best.orelse:
        old = "".join(lines[best.lineno - 1: best.end_lineno])
        indent = lines[best.lineno - 1][: len(lines[best.lineno - 1]) - len(lines[best.lineno - 1].lstrip())]
        rejects = all(isinstance(b, (ast.Raise, ast.Return)) for b in best.body)
        if rejects:
            return old, indent + "pass\n"
        body = "".join(lines[best.body[0].lineno - 1: best.body[-1].end_lineno])
        return old, textwrap.indent(textwrap.dedent(body), indent)
    old = "".join(lines[best.lineno - 1: best.end_lineno])
    indent = lines[best.lineno - 1][: len(lines[best.lineno - 1]) - len(lines[best.lineno - 1].lstrip())]
    return old, indent + "pass\n"


def counterfactuals(source: str, applied: str, note_text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Every counterfactual edit for the note's applied line: the statement-level one (auto_revert) and,
    for each call in the line whose function the note names, the call replaced by its first argument
    (float(amount) -> amount, ensure_utc(at) -> at). The note is validated only if EVERY one of them makes
    a test of its conventions fail: a claim about a sub-expression is not validated by the statement."""
    import ast
    import re
    from .evidence import code_names
    edits = []
    words = {w for w in re.findall(r"\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\b", note_text)}
    stmt = auto_revert(source, applied, words)
    if stmt:
        edits.append(stmt)
    named = code_names(note_text) | {w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\b", note_text)}
    lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    target = " ".join(applied.split())
    idx = next((i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if target and target in " ".join(ln.split())), None)
    if idx is None:
        return edits
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):  # calls on the applied line, inside whatever statement holds it
        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and node.args and node.lineno - 1 == idx and node.end_lineno - 1 == idx:
            fn = node.func.attr if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) else getattr(node.func, "id", "")
            if fn.lower() in named and not isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
                call, arg = ast.get_source_segment(source, node), ast.get_source_segment(source, node.args[0])
                if call and arg and call in lines[idx]:
                    edits.append((lines[idx], lines[idx].replace(call, arg, 1)))
    return edits


def check_all(task, workspace: Path, file: str, edits, conventions: set[str]) -> dict:
    """Validated only if the change passes and every counterfactual edit breaks a test of the conventions."""
    if not edits:
        return {"status": "inconclusive: no counterfactual edit", "validated": False, "edits": []}
    results = [check(task, workspace, file, [e], conventions) for e in edits]
    ok = all(r["validated"] for r in results)
    return {"status": "validated" if ok else next(r["status"] for r in results if not r["validated"]),
            "validated": ok, "after_passed": results[0]["after_passed"], "edits": [r["status"] for r in results]}
attest/memory/earned.py:
"""Attest's memory: experience that is verified, scoped, versioned and retractable.

Design rules (each one is enforced by deterministic code; the model only proposes):

1. Write gate.   Only tasks whose final result passed verification may write memory.
                 Every candidate needs typed evidence (see evidence.py), recorded
                 separately: a SOURCE (verbatim excerpt of a review comment or the
                 diff, with any policy/incident references it names) and an APPLIED
                 line (a changed line of the verified diff, typed code/test/doc/config,
                 added or removed). A rule someone merely said, but the verified change
                 never did, is not learned (this also blocks poisoned review advice).
                 VERIFICATION (did the change pass) is a third field: passing tests show
                 the code meets the tests, not that the rule is right. An optional
                 independent review by a second model can be switched on (off in the
                 experiment). Rejected candidates stay in the log with the reason.
2. Scope.        Every item records the repository, the files it was observed in, the
                 version it was learned on and the versions it is valid for
                 (valid_from .. valid_until). Retrieval only considers items valid for
                 the task's repository and checked-out version.
3. Version.      Items learned on an older major version and not yet re-verified are
                 shown with a warning to check the CHANGELOG (validity unknown). Items
                 known to be invalid for this version are not shown.
4. Accounting.   Every time an item is shown or cited is recorded. If a task that
                 cited an item fails a review check about the same thing, the item
                 becomes "suspect"; a second such failure retires it. A later
                 verified success that cites it clears the suspicion. The latest
                 verification of every item is kept (last_verification).
5. Lifecycle.    When newer verified evidence changes a rule, the old item is marked
                 "superseded" and points to its replacement (never deleted):
                   - the rule changed in a newer version ("supersedes"): the old item
                     stays valid for older versions (valid_until = the new version),
                     the new one is valid from that version;
                   - the old rule was wrong ("corrects", or a change on the same
                     version): the old item is invalid everywhere.

Ablations (same class, one mechanism switched off; preregistered):
  gate=False   learn from every finished task, verified or not, and admit any
               well-formed candidate without evidence (rule 1 off)
  scope=False  retrieve across repositories and versions, no version ranges or
               warnings (rules 2-3 off)
Accounting and supersede (rules 4-5) stay on in both.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from .. import llm
from ..benchmark import Task
from .base import MemorySystem, Retrieved, experience_packet
from .evidence import applied_is_relevant, find_applied, parse_diff, references, source_corpus
from .secrets import find_secrets, redact, redact_obj
from .retrieval import check_retriever, timed_rank
from .sqlite_store import open_store
from .text import jaccard, normalise, related

MAX_SHOWN = 6        # notes injected into the prompt
MAX_RETRIEVED = 10   # notes ranked and recorded as retrieved (the first MAX_SHOWN are injected)
VISIBLE = ("active", "suspect")
TYPES = ("business_policy", "code_convention", "process", "lesson")

DISTILL_SYSTEM = """You turn a finished coding task into reusable experience for FUTURE tasks in the SAME repository.

Return JSON: {"candidates": [...]} with at most 3 candidates. Each candidate has:
  "kind": "project_fact" (how this repository works) or "lesson" (how to work in it),
  "type": "business_policy" (a rule set by a policy, incident or finance/legal decision), "code_convention" (how code is
          written here), "process" (docs, changelog, tests or review practice) or "lesson",
  "topic": short kebab-case label, e.g. "money-rounding",
  "title": at most 8 words,
  "content": one or two imperative sentences a developer can act on; name the exact modules and functions,
  "evidence_quote": an exact, verbatim excerpt (10-200 characters) copied from the REVIEW COMMENTS or the FINAL DIFF that proves the candidate,
  "applied_in_diff": an exact, verbatim piece (10-200 characters) of one changed line of the FINAL DIFF where the accepted change
                     applies this rule: an added line ("+"), or a removed line ("-") if the rule is about removing something.

Rules:
- Only include knowledge specific to this repository that the issue text alone would not tell a competent developer.
- Do not restate the issue or describe this task's feature.
- Prefer what the review comments corrected.
- Only include rules that the accepted change actually applies; if you cannot point to a changed line that applies it, leave it out.
- If nothing qualifies, return {"candidates": []}."""

# Optional variant (D46; off in the experiment): after the Saleor coverage funnel, notes are written as
# the general rule plus the example it was learned from, and marked repository-wide or local.
DISTILL_GENERAL_SYSTEM = DISTILL_SYSTEM.replace(
    """  "content": one or two imperative sentences a developer can act on; name the exact modules and functions,""",
    """  "content": one or two imperative sentences stating the RULE as it applies across this repository, so that it can be
             recognised in a change to a different feature; name modules, functions or files only when the rule is about them,
  "example": one line: where this task applied the rule (file, function), for illustration,
  "breadth": "repository" if the rule applies to most changes of this repository (e.g. changelog, tests, typing, naming,
             migrations, API compatibility), "local" if it applies only to one module or feature,""")

RELATE_SYSTEM = """You compare a NEW piece of repository experience with EXISTING items from the same repository.
For each existing item decide how the NEW one relates to it:
  "duplicate"  - states the same rule,
  "supersedes" - is about the same rule, which CHANGED (e.g. a new version or a new policy changed it; the old one was right before),
  "corrects"   - is about the same rule and shows the old item was WRONG,
  "unrelated"  - a different topic.
Return JSON: {"relations": [{"id": "<existing id>", "relation": "duplicate|supersedes|corrects|unrelated"}]}"""

REVIEW_SYSTEM = """You review a note that a coding agent wants to keep as experience for future work in one repository.
Accept it only if it is a reusable rule of this repository (not a one-off detail of the change), it is supported by the
quoted evidence, and the stated scope is right. Return JSON: {"verdict": "accept" | "reject", "reason": "<one line>"}"""


def _major(version: str) -> str:
    return version.split(".")[0]


def _version_tuple(version: str) -> tuple:
    return tuple(int(p) if p.isdigit() else 0 for p in version.split("."))


def validity(item: dict, version: str | None) -> str:
    """"" if the item may be used on this version, otherwise why not (for the retrieval trace)."""
    status, scope = item.get("status"), item.get("scope", {})
    if status == "retired":
        return "retired" + (f" by {item['retracted_by']}" if item.get("retracted_by") else "")
    if status == "superseded" and not scope.get("valid_until"):
        if item.get("supersede"):  # D69: replaced by a newer approved rule (e.g. a policy change), not necessarily wrong
            return f"superseded by {item.get('superseded_by')} (replaced by a newer rule, recorded by {item['supersede'].get('by')})"
        return f"superseded by {item.get('superseded_by')} (the old rule was wrong)"
    if version is not None:
        if scope.get("valid_from") and _version_tuple(version) < _version_tuple(scope["valid_from"]):
            return f"not yet effective: valid from {scope['valid_from']}"
        if scope.get("valid_until") and _version_tuple(version) >= _version_tuple(scope["valid_until"]):
            return f"superseded by {item.get('superseded_by')} from {scope['valid_until']}"
    if status not in VISIBLE and status != "superseded":
        return f"status {status}"
    return ""


class EarnedMemory(MemorySystem):
    def __init__(self, store_dir: Path | None, *, gate: bool = True, scope: bool = True, backend: str | None = None,
                 retriever: str = "lexical", review_model: str | None = None, relevance: bool = False,
                 secret_scan: bool = False, general: bool = False, reserved: int = 0):
        self.store = open_store(store_dir, backend)
        self.gate, self.scope = gate, scope
        self.review_model = review_model  # optional independent review in the write gate (off in the experiment)
        self.relevance = relevance  # optional: the applied line must name code the evidence quote names (D37; off in the experiment)
        self.secret_scan = secret_scan  # optional: reject or redact credentials before anything is stored (D43; off in the experiment)
        self.general = general  # optional: notes as a general rule + example, marked repository-wide or local (D46; off)
        self.reserved = reserved  # optional: injection slots kept for repository-wide rules, most-confirmed first (D46; 0 = off)
        self.retriever = check_retriever(retriever)
        self.name = ("attest" + ("" if gate else "_no_gate") + ("" if scope else "_no_scope")
                     + {"embedding": "_emb", "hybrid": "_hybrid", "hybrid_rerank": "_hybrid_rerank"}.get(retriever, "")
                     + ("_general" if general else ""))

    def _same_scope(self, item: dict, task: Task) -> bool:
        return not self.scope or item["scope"]["repo"] == task.repo_name

    def _exclusion(self, item: dict, task: Task, version: str | None) -> str:
        """Why an item may not be used for this task ("" if it may)."""
        if not self._same_scope(item, task):
            return f"other repository: {item['scope']['repo']}"
        if not self.scope:  # ablation: no version ranges, only the status counts
            return "" if item["status"] in VISIBLE else f"status {item['status']}"
        return validity(item, version)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ read path

    def candidates(self, task: Task, version: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
        """The notes retrieval may choose from (valid for this repository and version), as id -> text to rank."""
        return {i: f"{it['title']} {it['content']}" for i, it in self.store.items().items()
                if not self._exclusion(it, task, version)}

    def ranking(self, task: Task, k: int | None = MAX_SHOWN, version: str | None = None) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, float]], float]:
        """(ranked candidates, milliseconds). Only this step differs between the retrieval arms."""
        cands = self.candidates(task, version)
        details = None
        if self.retriever == "hybrid_rerank":  # applicability conditions for the reranker (D47)
            items = self.store.items()
            details = {i: f"type {items[i].get('type')}; learned in {', '.join(items[i]['scope'].get('files') or []) or 'no file'}; "
                          f"holds for {_range(items[i]['scope'])}" for i in cands}
        return timed_rank(self.retriever, f"{task.title} {task.issue}", cands, k, details)

    def _reserve(self, task: Task, version: str, ranked: list) -> list:
        """Keep up to self.reserved of the injected slots for repository-wide rules (D46), most
        independent tasks first, then by relevance; the remaining slots go by relevance as before."""
        items = self.store.items()
        score = dict(self.ranking(task, None, version)[0])
        wide = sorted((i for i in self.candidates(task, version) if items[i].get("breadth") == "repository"),
                      key=lambda i: (-len({e.get("task_id") for e in items[i]["evidence"]}), -score.get(i, 0.0), i))[: self.reserved]
        rest = [(i, sc) for i, sc in ranked if i not in wide]
        return [(i, score.get(i, 0.0)) for i in wide] + rest

    def retrieve(self, task: Task, repo_version: str) -> Retrieved:
        items = self.store.items()
        excluded = {i: why for i, it in items.items() if (why := self._exclusion(it, task, repo_version))}
        ranked, ms = self.ranking(task, MAX_RETRIEVED, repo_version)
        if self.reserved:
            ranked = self._reserve(task, repo_version, ranked)
        chosen = [items[i] for i, _ in ranked[:getattr(self, "max_shown", MAX_SHOWN)]]  # D64: an arm may vary k
        version_warnings = [it["id"] for it in chosen
                            if self.scope and _major(it["scope"]["observed_version"]) != _major(repo_version)
                            and _major(it["scope"].get("revalidated_on") or it["scope"]["observed_version"]) != _major(repo_version)]
        debug = {
            "in_scope": sorted(i for i, it in items.items() if self._same_scope(it, task) and items[i]["status"] in VISIBLE),
            "out_of_scope": sorted(i for i, it in items.items() if not self._same_scope(it, task) and it["status"] in VISIBLE),
            "not_visible": sorted(i for i in excluded if self._same_scope(items[i], task) or items[i]["status"] not in VISIBLE),
            "scores": dict(ranked),
            "retriever": self.retriever,
            "retrieval_ms": ms,
            "version_warnings": version_warnings,
        }
        lines = []
        if chosen:
            lines.append("These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. "
                         "Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.")
        for it in chosen:
            u, sc = it["usage"], it["scope"]
            lines.append(f"- [{it['id']}] {it['title']}: {it['content']}" + (f" (example: {it['example']})" if it.get("example") else ""))
            valid = f"valid from {sc['valid_from']}" if sc.get("valid_from") and sc["valid_from"] != sc["observed_version"] else ""
            refs = ", ".join((it.get("source") or {}).get("references") or [])
            lines.append(
                f"  (learned from task {it['source']['task_id']} on {sc['repo']} {sc['observed_version']}"
                f"{'; ' + valid if valid else ''}{'; source ' + refs if refs else ''}; "
                f"relied on {u['cited']}x, {u['cited_pass']} passed, {u['cited_fail']} failed)"
            )
            if it["status"] == "suspect":
                lines.append("  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.")
            if it["id"] in version_warnings:
                lines.append(
                    f"  WARNING: learned on version {sc['observed_version']}, this checkout is {repo_version}. "
                    "Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it."
                )
        context = "\n".join(lines)
        debug["trace"] = {
            "excluded": excluded,
            "candidates": len(items) - len(excluded),
            "retrieved": [i for i, _ in ranked],
            "injected": [it["id"] for it in chosen],
            "memory_tokens_approx": len(context) // 4,
            "texts": {i: f"{it['title']} {it['content']}"[:300] for i, it in items.items()},
        }
        return Retrieved(ids=[it["id"] for it in chosen], context=context, debug=debug)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ usage accounting

    def feedback(self, task: Task, repo_version: str, run: dict) -> list[dict]:
        items = self.store.items()
        first = run["attempts"][0]
        cited = set(run["cited_notes"]) & set(run["shown_notes"])
        events = []
        for item_id in run["shown_notes"]:
            it = items.get(item_id)
            if not it:
                continue
            usage = dict(it["usage"], shown=it["usage"]["shown"] + 1)
            fields, reason = {"usage": usage}, f"shown in {task.id}"
            if item_id in cited:
                usage["cited"] += 1
                note_text = f"{it['title']} {it['content']}"
                blame = [c for c in first["review_comments"] if related(note_text, c)]
                if first["passed"]:
                    usage["cited_pass"] += 1
                    usage["fail_streak"] = 0
                    reason = f"cited in {task.id}, which passed"
                    fields["last_verification"] = {"task_id": task.id, "version": repo_version, "result": "passed",
                                                   "how": "cited by a task whose first attempt passed verification"}
                    if it["status"] == "suspect":
                        fields["status"] = "active"
                        reason += "; suspicion cleared"
                    if _major(it["scope"]["observed_version"]) != _major(repo_version):
                        fields["scope"] = dict(it["scope"], revalidated_on=repo_version)
                elif blame:
                    usage["cited_fail"] += 1
                    usage["fail_streak"] += 1
                    fields["status"] = "suspect" if usage["fail_streak"] == 1 else "retired"
                    fields["last_failure"] = {"task_id": task.id, "review_comment": blame[0]}
                    fields["last_verification"] = {"task_id": task.id, "version": repo_version, "result": "failed",
                                                   "how": "cited by a task that failed a related review check",
                                                   "review_comment": blame[0]}
                    reason = f"cited in {task.id}, which failed a related review check -> {fields['status']}"
                else:
                    reason = f"cited in {task.id}, which failed for an unrelated reason (no blame)"
            events.append(self.store.append("update", id=item_id, fields=fields, reason=reason))
        return events

    def retract(self, item_id: str, reason: str, by: str = "human") -> dict:
        """A person withdraws a note. It stays in the log as retired, with who and why."""
        if item_id not in self.store.items():
            raise KeyError(item_id)
        return self.store.append("update", id=item_id, fields={"status": "retired", "retracted_by": by},
                                 reason=f"retracted by {by}: {reason}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write path

    def learn(self, task: Task, repo_version: str, run: dict, transcript: str, diff: str,
              candidates: list[dict] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        """Distill (or accept proposed) candidates and admit those that pass the gate.

        ``candidates`` lets a caller that is itself a model (e.g. an agent using the MCP
        server) propose notes; they go through exactly the same gate."""
        if self.gate and not run["final_pass"]:
            return [self.store.append("reject", task_id=task.id, candidate=None, reason="task not verified: nothing is learned")]
        data = ({"candidates": candidates} if candidates is not None
                else llm.complete_json(DISTILL_GENERAL_SYSTEM if self.general else DISTILL_SYSTEM,
                                       experience_packet(task, repo_version, run, transcript, diff)))
        comments = run["attempts"][0]["review_comments"]
        corpus, changed = source_corpus(comments, diff), parse_diff(diff)
        events = []
        for cand in (data.get("candidates") or [])[:3]:
            problem = self._gate(cand, corpus, changed, require_evidence=self.gate)
            if not problem and self.gate and self.relevance:
                applied = find_applied(cand.get("applied_in_diff") or "", changed)
                if applied_is_relevant(cand.get("evidence_quote") or "", (applied or {}).get("line", "")) is False:
                    problem = "applied line is unrelated to the evidence: it names none of the code the quote names"
            if not problem and self.gate and self.review_model:
                problem = self._independent_review(task, cand)
            if not problem and self.secret_scan:
                kinds = find_secrets(f"{cand.get('title') or ''} {cand.get('content') or ''}")
                if kinds:
                    problem = f"contains a secret ({', '.join(kinds)}): never stored as experience"
            if problem:
                stored = redact_obj(cand) if self.secret_scan else cand
                events.append(self.store.append("reject", task_id=task.id, candidate=stored, reason=problem))
                continue
            if self.secret_scan:  # the gate checked the originals; only redacted text is stored
                run_r = dict(run, attempts=[dict(run["attempts"][0], review_comments=redact_obj(comments))] + list(run["attempts"][1:]))
                events.extend(self._admit(task, repo_version, run_r, redact_obj(cand), parse_diff(redact(diff))))
                continue
            events.extend(self._admit(task, repo_version, run, cand, changed))
        return events

    @staticmethod
    def _gate(cand: dict, corpus: str, changed: list, require_evidence: bool = True) -> str:
        if not isinstance(cand, dict):
            return "malformed candidate"
        if cand.get("kind") in TYPES and cand.get("kind") != "lesson":  # the model put the type into "kind"
            cand.setdefault("type", cand["kind"])
            cand["kind"] = "project_fact"
        if cand.get("kind") not in ("project_fact", "lesson"):
            return f"unknown kind {cand.get('kind')!r}"
        content = (cand.get("content") or "").strip()
        if not 20 <= len(content) <= 400:
            return "content must be 20-400 characters"
        if not require_evidence:
            return ""
        quote = normalise(cand.get("evidence_quote") or "")
        if len(quote) < 10:
            return "missing evidence quote"
        if quote not in corpus:
            return "source: evidence quote not found verbatim in the review comments or the diff"
        if find_applied(cand.get("applied_in_diff") or "", changed) is None:
            return "not applied in the verified change: no changed line of the diff matches applied_in_diff"
        return ""

    def _independent_review(self, task: Task, cand: dict) -> str:
        prompt = json.dumps({"repository": task.repo_name, "note": {k: cand.get(k) for k in ("title", "content", "type")},
                             "evidence_quote": cand.get("evidence_quote"), "applied_in_diff": cand.get("applied_in_diff")},
                            ensure_ascii=False)
        verdict = llm.complete_json(REVIEW_SYSTEM, prompt, model=self.review_model)
        cand["_review"] = {"model": self.review_model, "verdict": verdict.get("verdict"), "reason": verdict.get("reason", "")}
        return "" if verdict.get("verdict") == "accept" else f"independent review rejected it: {verdict.get('reason', '')}"

    @staticmethod
    def _evidence(task: Task, repo_version: str, run: dict, cand: dict, changed: list) -> dict:
        quote = cand.get("evidence_quote") or ""
        comments = run["attempts"][0]["review_comments"]
        from_review = next((c for c in comments if normalise(quote) and normalise(quote) in normalise(c)), None)
        return {
            "task_id": task.id,
            "version": repo_version,
            "source": {"kind": "review_comment" if from_review else ("diff" if quote else "none"), "quote": quote,
                       "references": references(quote, from_review or ""),
                       # D61: the whole comment the quote came from, so later evidence can be traced to its origin
                       **({"comment": from_review} if from_review else {})},
            "applied": find_applied(cand.get("applied_in_diff") or "", changed),
            "verification": {"passed": bool(run["final_pass"]), "first_pass": bool(run["first_pass"]),
                             "how": run.get("verified_by", "hidden tests")},
            "independent_review": cand.get("_review"),
        }

    def _admit(self, task: Task, repo_version: str, run: dict, cand: dict, changed: list) -> list[dict]:
        items = self.store.items()
        # Items this one may duplicate or replace: same repository, still in use for some version.
        existing = [it for it in items.values() if self._same_scope(it, task)
                    and (it["status"] in VISIBLE or it["status"] in ("archived", "quarantined")
                         or (it["status"] == "superseded" and it["scope"].get("valid_until")))]
        relations = {}
        if existing:
            listing = [{"id": it["id"], "title": it["title"], "content": it["content"],
                        "versions": _range(it["scope"])} for it in existing]
            prompt = json.dumps({"new": {"title": cand.get("title"), "content": cand["content"], "version": repo_version},
                                 "existing": listing}, ensure_ascii=False)
            try:
                data = llm.complete_json(RELATE_SYSTEM, prompt)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no model available: fall back to lexical duplicate detection
                data = {"relations": [{"id": it["id"], "relation": "duplicate"} for it in existing
                                      if jaccard(cand["content"], it["content"]) >= 0.6]}
            relations = {r.get("id"): r.get("relation") for r in data.get("relations") or [] if isinstance(r, dict)}
        evidence = self._evidence(task, repo_version, run, cand, changed)
        verification = {"task_id": task.id, "version": repo_version, "result": "passed" if run["final_pass"] else "unverified",
                        "how": f"learned from a task whose final change {'passed' if run['final_pass'] else 'did not pass'} verification"}

        # A quarantined note must not come back as a "new" note (D45). A note that corrects or
        # replaces it is learned normally and never replaces it automatically (see below).
        held = next((it for it in existing if it["status"] == "quarantined" and relations.get(it["id"]) == "duplicate"), None)
        if held:
            return [self.store.append("reject", task_id=task.id, candidate=cand,
                                      reason=f"repeats quarantined note {held['id']}: held until a person reviews it")]
        duplicate = next((it for it in existing if relations.get(it["id"]) == "duplicate"
                          and (it["status"] == "archived" or not validity(it, repo_version))), None)
        if duplicate:
            fields = {
                "evidence": duplicate["evidence"] + [evidence],
                "usage": dict(duplicate["usage"], fail_streak=0),
                "status": "active",
                "last_verification": verification,
            }
            was = " (reactivated from the archive)" if duplicate["status"] == "archived" else ""
            return [self.store.append("update", id=duplicate["id"], fields=fields, candidate=cand,
                                      reason=f"confirmed again by verified task {task.id}{was}")]

        # Only newer (or same-version) verified evidence may replace an older rule.
        replaced = [
            it for it in existing
            if relations.get(it["id"]) in ("supersedes", "corrects") and it["status"] != "quarantined"
            and _version_tuple(repo_version) >= _version_tuple(it["scope"]["observed_version"])
        ]
        changes = {it["id"]: ("version" if relations[it["id"]] == "supersedes"
                              and _version_tuple(repo_version) > _version_tuple(it["scope"]["observed_version"]) else "correction")
                   for it in replaced}
        new_id = self.store.next_id("at")
        applied = evidence["applied"]
        corrected_from = [it["scope"].get("valid_from") or it["scope"]["observed_version"] for it in replaced if changes[it["id"]] == "correction"]
        item = {
            "id": new_id,
            "kind": cand["kind"],
            "type": cand.get("type") if cand.get("type") in TYPES else ("lesson" if cand["kind"] == "lesson" else "code_convention"),
            "topic": cand.get("topic", ""),
            "title": (cand.get("title") or cand["content"][:40]).strip(),
            "content": cand["content"].strip(),
            **({"example": str(cand.get("example") or "").strip()[:300],
                "breadth": cand.get("breadth") if cand.get("breadth") in ("repository", "local") else "local"} if self.general else {}),
            "scope": {"repo": task.repo_name, "observed_version": repo_version,
                      # a correction inherits the range of the rule it fixes; a changed rule starts at this version
                      "valid_from": min(corrected_from, key=_version_tuple) if corrected_from else repo_version,
                      "valid_until": None, "files": [applied["file"]] if applied else []},
            "source": {"task_id": task.id, "first_pass": run["first_pass"], "review_comments": run["attempts"][0]["review_comments"],
                       "references": evidence["source"]["references"],
                       "proposed_by": run.get("proposed_by") or "agent:distiller"},  # D62: who proposed it (never its approver)
            "evidence": [evidence],
            "status": "active",
            "supersedes": [it["id"] for it in replaced],
            "superseded_by": None,
            "last_verification": verification,
            "usage": {"shown": 0, "cited": 0, "cited_pass": 0, "cited_fail": 0, "fail_streak": 0},
        }
        events = [self.store.append("add", item=item, reason=f"distilled from verified task {task.id}")]
        for old in replaced:
            if changes[old["id"]] == "version":
                fields = {"status": "superseded", "superseded_by": new_id, "supersede_kind": "rule changed",
                          "scope": dict(old["scope"], valid_until=repo_version)}
                reason = (f"rule changed: {new_id} applies from {task.repo_name} {repo_version}; "
                          f"this item stays valid for {_range(fields['scope'])}")
            else:
                fields = {"status": "superseded", "superseded_by": new_id, "supersede_kind": "corrected",
                          "scope": dict(old["scope"], valid_until=None)}
                reason = f"corrected by {new_id} from verified task {task.id} on {task.repo_name} {repo_version}"
            events.append(self.store.append("update", id=old["id"], fields=fields, reason=reason))
        return events


def _range(scope: dict) -> str:
    start = scope.get("valid_from") or scope.get("observed_version")
    return f">= {start}" + (f", < {scope['valid_until']}" if scope.get("valid_until") else "")
attest/memory/forgetting.py:
"""Dynamic forgetting V1 for Attest (exploratory, after the main experiment).

Two layers, in this order:
  1. Eligibility (unchanged, deterministic): repository scope, version range and
     lifecycle status decide whether a note may be used at all (earned.validity).
     Forgetting never overrides them: an outdated rule is excluded because its
     version range ended, not because it decayed.
  2. Retention (this module): among eligible notes, which are still worth keeping
     in active memory. Low-value notes are *archived*, never deleted: they stay in
     the append-only log with their scores, are no longer retrieved, and are
     reactivated when a new verified task yields the same rule again.

Retention of a note:  R = E * max(D, U)
  E  evidence quality: 1.0 source names a policy or incident (FIN-, INC-), 0.7 a
     review comment, 0.5 only the diff, 0.3 no applied evidence
  U  verified utility: 1 - 0.5**k, k = distinct tasks in which the note was used
     and the task passed (repeats of the same task count once)
  D  decay, by policy:
       uniform     2**(-age / 50), age = tasks since the note was last verified
       type_aware  half-life by type: business_policy never decays, code_convention
                   200, process 100, lesson 50 tasks (wall-clock age as above)
       exposure    2**(-unused / 10), unused = times the note was injected since
                   its last verified use without being used; a note no task needed
                   is never injected and so never decays
       none        no forgetting
  A note is archived when R < 0.2 (and it is active or suspect).

The numbers are first-version assumptions, not tuned values.

V1.1 (opt-in through `params` and `observe(verified=...)`; V1 stays the default):
  - V1 lets one verified use protect a note for ever (U >= 0.5, so R >= 0.25 > 0.2).
    With utility_factor, U also decays, that many times slower than D.
  - A note's progress is recorded in stages: injected, adopted (used), behaviour
    verified. Only verified use reinforces; "the task passed" alone does not.
  - protect_cited: a note citing a policy or incident (FIN-, POL-, SEC-, INC-) never decays,
    whatever its type label. Added to the type protection (business_policy never decays
    under type_aware), not a replacement for it.
  - utility_factor = 4 is an experimental setting; 2 and 8 are reported beside it.
  - Fix, for V1 too: reactivation resets the decay clock, so a note restored by new
    evidence is not archived again at the next maintenance. (No published run reactivated
    a note: the streams never re-learn, and end-to-end runs do not update memory.)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

POLICIES = ("none", "uniform", "type_aware", "exposure", "exposure_ranked")
TYPE_HALF_LIFE = {"business_policy": None, "code_convention": 200, "process": 100, "lesson": 50}
UNIFORM_HALF_LIFE = 50
EXPOSURE_HALF_LIFE = 10
THRESHOLD = 0.2
ACTIVE = ("active", "suspect")


def evidence_quality(item: dict) -> float:
    ev = (item.get("evidence") or [{}])[0]
    src, applied = ev.get("source") or {}, ev.get("applied")
    from . import admission

    if not applied:
        return 0.3
    if any(r.split("-", 1)[0] in admission.POLICY_PREFIXES for r in src.get("references") or []):
        return 1.0
    return 0.7 if src.get("kind") == "review_comment" else 0.5


def _track(item: dict) -> dict:
    return dict(item.get("forgetting") or {"last_verified_tick": item.get("created_tick", 0),
                                            "unused_exposures": 0, "verified_tasks": []})


def retention(item: dict, now: int, policy: str, params: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """params: half_life (uniform), type_scale (type_aware: multiplies every finite type half-life),
    exposure_half_life (sensitivity analysis); utility_factor (V1.1): if set, historical utility U
    also decays, `utility_factor` times slower than D, so a note used once is not kept forever;
    policy rules (no finite half-life) keep their utility. protect_cited (V1.1): a note whose
    evidence cites a policy or incident (admission.POLICY_PREFIXES) never decays either, whatever
    type the distiller gave it (it typed the same idempotency rule `process` in two repetitions
    and `business_policy` in the third). This is added to the type protection, not a
    replacement: under type_aware a note typed business_policy still never decays, cited or
    not. The utility_factor value (4) is an experimental setting, not a tuned optimum.
    Defaults are V1, fixed before any run."""
    from . import admission

    params = params or {}
    t = _track(item)
    e = evidence_quality(item)
    k = len(set(t["verified_tasks"]) | set(t.get("demand_tasks") or []))  # demand: V2, empty otherwise
    u = 1 - 0.5 ** k
    age = max(0, now - t["last_verified_tick"])
    clock, half = age, None  # the quantity D decays over, and its half-life
    if policy == "uniform":
        half = params.get("half_life", UNIFORM_HALF_LIFE)
    elif policy == "type_aware":
        half = TYPE_HALF_LIFE.get(item.get("type") or "lesson", 50)
        half = None if half is None else half * params.get("type_scale", 1.0)
    elif policy in ("exposure", "exposure_ranked"):
        clock, half = t["unused_exposures"], params.get("exposure_half_life", EXPOSURE_HALF_LIFE)
    if params.get("protect_cited") and admission.policy_references(item):
        half = None
    if params.get("stability") and half is not None:
        # V2: no utility floor. Each independent verified (or demanded) task multiplies the
        # half-life by `stability`, as in spaced repetition: a detail verified once still fades.
        half = half * params["stability"] ** k
        d = 2 ** (-clock / half)
        return {"E": round(e, 3), "U": round(u, 3), "D": round(d, 3), "R": round(e * d, 3), "age": age,
                "unused_exposures": t["unused_exposures"], "verified_tasks": k, "half_life": half}
    d = 1.0 if half is None else 2 ** (-clock / half)
    if params.get("utility_factor") and half is not None:
        u *= 2 ** (-clock / (half * params["utility_factor"]))
    return {"E": round(e, 3), "U": round(u, 3), "D": round(d, 3), "R": round(e * max(d, u), 3), "age": age,
            "unused_exposures": t["unused_exposures"], "verified_tasks": k}


def observe(memory, tick: int, task_id: str, injected: list[str], used: list[str], passed: bool,
            verified: list[str] | None = None, *, negative=(), demand=(), relevant=None) -> None:
    """After a task, record how far each note got: retrieved, injected, adopted (used), verified.

    V1 (verified=None): a note used in a passing task is reinforced.
    V1.1 (verified given): only notes whose related behaviour was checked and passed (e.g. the
    hidden test of the note's convention) are reinforced; a note adopted in a passing task whose
    behaviour nobody checked is counted as adopted but not reinforced ("the task passed" is not
    "this note contributed"). Injected notes that were not used gain an unused exposure.

    V2, each optional and empty by default (V1 and V1.1 behave as before):
      negative  notes adopted in this task whose related check then failed: negative evidence
      demand    notes about a convention this task needed and failed without (the review or the
                test named it): positive evidence although they were not injected; an archived
                or dormant note is reactivated, with its clock reset
      relevant  if given, an injected but unused note gains an unused exposure only when it is
                in this list (the task touches the note's files), not for every injection"""
    items = memory.store.items()
    reinforce = set(used) if verified is None else set(verified)
    for i in set(injected) | set(used) | reinforce | set(negative) | set(demand):
        if i not in items:
            continue
        it, fields = items[i], {}
        t = _track(it)
        if i in negative:
            t["negative"] = t.get("negative", 0) + 1
            reason = f"adopted in {task_id}, and its check failed (tick {tick})"
        elif i in demand:
            if it.get("status") in ("retired", "superseded") or t.get("negative", 0) > 0:
                # eligibility first: demand never revives a retracted or replaced rule, nor one
                # whose check failed after it was followed (negative evidence outranks demand)
                continue
            t["demand_tasks"] = sorted(set(t.get("demand_tasks") or []) | {task_id})
            t["last_verified_tick"], t["unused_exposures"] = tick, 0
            reason = f"needed in {task_id}: its convention failed without it (tick {tick})"
            if it.get("status") in ("archived", "dormant"):
                fields["status"] = "active"
                reason += "; reactivated"
        elif i in used and i not in reinforce:
            t["adopted_unverified"] = t.get("adopted_unverified", 0) + 1
            reason = f"adopted in {task_id}, behaviour not verified (tick {tick})"
        elif i in reinforce and passed:
            t["verified_tasks"] = sorted(set(t["verified_tasks"]) | {task_id})
            t["last_verified_tick"], t["unused_exposures"] = tick, 0
            reason = f"used in {task_id}, which passed (tick {tick})"
            if it.get("status") == "dormant":
                fields["status"] = "active"
                reason += "; woken from dormant"
        elif i in injected and i not in used:
            if relevant is not None and i not in relevant:
                continue
            t["unused_exposures"] += 1
            reason = f"injected in {task_id} but not used (tick {tick})"
        else:
            continue
        fields["forgetting"] = t
        memory.store.append("update", id=i, fields=fields, reason=reason)


def maintain(memory, now: int, policy: str, threshold: float = THRESHOLD, params: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Archive active notes whose retention fell below the threshold. Returns the archive events.

    V2 (params["dormant"]): three evidence states. A note with negative evidence is archived; a
    note whose retention fell below the threshold without negative evidence becomes *dormant*
    (still injected where it was learned, woken by verified use or demand), because "no one
    used it lately" is not "it is wrong"."""
    if policy == "none":
        return []
    events = []
    for i, it in memory.store.items().items():
        if (params or {}).get("dormant"):
            if it.get("status") in (*ACTIVE, "dormant") and _track(it).get("negative", 0) > 0:
                events.append(memory.store.append("update", id=i, fields={"status": "archived", "archived": {"tick": now, "why": "negative evidence"}},
                                                  reason=f"archived at tick {now}: its check failed after it was adopted"))
                continue
            if it.get("status") not in ACTIVE:
                continue
            r = retention(it, now, policy, params)
            if r["R"] < threshold:
                events.append(memory.store.append("update", id=i, fields={"status": "dormant", "dormant": {"tick": now, **r}},
                                                  reason=f"dormant at tick {now}: R={r['R']}, no negative evidence"))
            continue
        if it.get("status") not in ACTIVE:
            continue
        r = retention(it, now, policy, params)
        if r["R"] < threshold:
            events.append(memory.store.append(
                "update", id=i, fields={"status": "archived", "archived": {"tick": now, "policy": policy, **r}},
                reason=f"archived by {policy} forgetting at tick {now}: R={r['R']} (E={r['E']}, D={r['D']}, U={r['U']})"))
    return events


def reset_track(item: dict, now: int, task_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """The forgetting state after reactivation: verified now, no unused exposures. Without this a
    reactivated note keeps its old age and is archived again at the next maintenance."""
    t = _track(item)
    t["last_verified_tick"], t["unused_exposures"] = now, 0
    if task_id:
        t["verified_tasks"] = sorted(set(t["verified_tasks"]) | {task_id})
    return t


def reactivate(memory, item_id: str, reason: str, now: int, task_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """A person, or a new verified task yielding the same rule, brings an archived note back.

    `now` (the current task clock) is required: reactivation always resets the decay clock,
    otherwise the note keeps its old age and is archived again at the next maintenance."""
    if not isinstance(now, int):
        raise TypeError("reactivate needs the current task clock `now`")
    fields = {"status": "active", "forgetting": reset_track(memory.store.items()[item_id], now, task_id)}
    return memory.store.append("update", id=item_id, fields=fields, reason=f"reactivated: {reason}")


def half_life_note() -> str:
    return (f"uniform {UNIFORM_HALF_LIFE} tasks; type-aware {TYPE_HALF_LIFE}; exposure {EXPOSURE_HALF_LIFE} unused "
            f"injections; archive below R = {THRESHOLD}")


class ForgettingMemory:
    """Attest with a forgetting policy and, optionally, trust-tiered admission (admission.py).

    `exposure_ranked` ranks eligible notes by lexical relevance x (0.5 + 0.5 * retention).
    `tiered=True` excludes candidates outside their files and ranks rules before candidates.
    Other settings keep Attest's ranking."""

    def __new__(cls, store_dir, policy: str, now_fn, tiered: bool = False, trust=None):
        from . import admission
        from .earned import EarnedMemory
        from .retrieval import timed_rank

        class _Memory(EarnedMemory):
            def _admit(self, task, repo_version, run, cand, changed):
                events = super()._admit(task, repo_version, run, cand, changed)
                for e in list(events):  # a verified task confirmed an archived note: restart its clock
                    if e["type"] == "update" and "reactivated from the archive" in e.get("reason", ""):
                        t = reset_track(self.store.items()[e["id"]], now_fn(), task.id)
                        events.append(self.store.append("update", id=e["id"], fields={"forgetting": t},
                                                        reason=f"forgetting clock reset on reactivation (tick {now_fn()})"))
                return events

            def _exclusion(self, item, task, version):
                if item.get("status") == "dormant":  # V2: eligible like an active note, but only in its own files
                    why = super()._exclusion(dict(item, status="active"), task, version)
                    files = set((item.get("scope") or {}).get("files") or [])
                    return why or ("" if files & admission.files_named(task) else "dormant: injected only in its own files")
                why = super()._exclusion(item, task, version)
                if why or not tiered or admission.injectable_here(item, task, trust):
                    return why
                return "candidate: seen once, injected only in its own files"

            def ranking(self, task, k=6, version=None):
                if policy != "exposure_ranked" and not tiered:
                    return super().ranking(task, k, version)
                items = self.store.items()
                scored, ms = timed_rank("lexical", f"{task.title} {task.issue}", self.candidates(task, version), None)
                if policy == "exposure_ranked":
                    now = now_fn()
                    scored = [(i, round(sc * (0.5 + 0.5 * retention(items[i], now, policy)["R"]), 3)) for i, sc in scored]
                if tiered:  # tier first (rules with any relevance, then candidates), relevance within a tier
                    key = lambda x: (0 if x[1] > 0 and admission.tier(items[x[0]], trust) in admission.RULE_TIERS else 1 if x[1] > 0 else 2, -x[1], x[0])  # noqa: E731
                else:
                    key = lambda x: (-x[1], x[0])  # noqa: E731
                ranked = sorted(scored, key=key)
                return (ranked if k is None else ranked[:k]), ms

        memory = _Memory(store_dir)
        memory.name = f"attest_forget_{policy}" + ("_tiered" if tiered else "")
        return memory
attest/memory/governance.py:
"""Semantic governance of candidate notes (exploratory, D39): conflict detection with cited evidence.

The write gate checks provenance (the advice came from review, was applied, the task passed).
The second poison showed that this cannot stop wrong advice that is followed and passes the
tests. This module adds a check of whether a candidate is consistent with what the team already
holds, before it can be injected:

  sources   only the existing active rules of the same repository (with ids) and the
            repository's CHANGELOG at the current version. The reviewer may not rely on its own
            idea of good practice.
  verdicts  approved   no source contradicts it (or a CHANGELOG entry supports a changed rule)
            conflict   an existing rule or the CHANGELOG says the opposite for the same situation
            uncertain  the sources do not settle it
  citations a conflict must quote both sides verbatim (an excerpt of the source and of the
            candidate); quotes are checked deterministically, and a conflict whose quotes are
            not found is downgraded to uncertain. A claimed CHANGELOG support must be verbatim too.

A conflicting or uncertain candidate is stored with status "conflict" or "pending_review": not
injected, both sides' evidence kept, the existing rule untouched, nothing superseded. It is
never rejected automatically, because the new advice may reflect a real policy change; a person
decides with resolve() (not exposed to agents, like retraction).

The reviewer is a separate model (deepseek-v4-pro by default, the judge model of the
retrospective), not the agent's model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from .. import llm
from ..benchmark import REPOS_DIR
from .earned import TYPES, VISIBLE, EarnedMemory
from .evidence import normalise

REVIEW_MODEL = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
HELD = ("conflict", "pending_review")

SEMANTIC_SYSTEM = """You check a candidate rule before it enters a software team's memory for one repository.
You may rely ONLY on the SOURCES given: the existing rules of this repository (each with an id) and the repository's
CHANGELOG. Do not use your own opinion of good practice, and do not reject a candidate only because it is unusual.

Decide one verdict:
  "approved"  - no source contradicts the candidate (also when a CHANGELOG entry at or before the current version
                explicitly supports a changed rule; then give that excerpt as "supported_by"),
  "conflict"  - an existing rule or the CHANGELOG says the opposite of the candidate for the same situation,
  "uncertain" - the sources do not let you decide.
For "conflict", quote the contradicting words EXACTLY: "source_id" is the existing rule's id or "CHANGELOG",
"source_quote" an exact excerpt (10-200 characters) copied from that source, "candidate_quote" an exact excerpt copied
from the candidate.

Return JSON: {"verdict": "approved|conflict|uncertain", "conflicts": [{"source_id": "...", "source_quote": "...",
"candidate_quote": "..."}], "supported_by": "<exact CHANGELOG excerpt or empty>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}"""


# Optional (D50): the reviewer may also cite the repository's current code. Excerpts are chosen
# deterministically (lines that name the code the candidate names), and a code citation must be
# found verbatim on the cited line, like every other citation.
CODE_SYSTEM = SEMANTIC_SYSTEM.replace(
    "the existing rules of this repository (each with an id) and the repository's\nCHANGELOG.",
    "the existing rules of this repository (each with an id), the repository's\nCHANGELOG, and CODE excerpts from the "
    "repository at the current version (each with an id \"code:<file>:<line>\"). Code is evidence of how the team\n"
    "actually works: a candidate that tells developers to do the opposite of what the code consistently enforces is a\n"
    "conflict, citing that code line.").replace(
    '"source_id" is the existing rule\'s id or "CHANGELOG"', '"source_id" is the existing rule\'s id, "CHANGELOG" or a code id')



def code_excerpts(repo: str, cand: dict, limit: int = 40) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Lines of the repository's code (tests included) that name the most identifiers the candidate names."""
    import re
    from .evidence import code_names
    text = " ".join(str(cand.get(k) or "") for k in ("title", "content", "evidence_quote"))
    names = code_names(text) | {w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\b(?:Decimal|float|int|str|round\w*|audit\w*|record|approved_by|idempotency_key|\w+Error)\b", text)}
    if not names:
        return {}
    root = REPOS_DIR / repo
    scored = []
    for f in sorted(root.rglob("*.py")):
        rel = f.relative_to(root)
        if "__pycache__" in rel.parts:
            continue
        for n, line in enumerate(f.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
            low = line.lower()
            hits = sum(1 for w in names if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(w)}\b", low))
            if hits and line.strip():
                scored.append((-hits, str(rel), n, line.strip()[:200]))
    scored.sort()
    return {f"code:{r}:{n}": l for _, r, n, l in scored[:limit]}


def changelog(repo: str) -> str:
    p = REPOS_DIR / repo / "CHANGELOG.md"
    return p.read_text() if p.exists() else ""


def _found(quote: str, text: str) -> bool:
    q = normalise(quote)
    return len(q) >= 10 and q in normalise(text)


def semantic_review(cand: dict, existing: list[dict], log: str, version: str, model: str | None = REVIEW_MODEL,
                    code: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict:
    """The reviewer's verdict, with its citations checked against the sources (and code, if given; D50)."""
    sources = {it["id"]: f"{it['title']}: {it['content']}" for it in existing}
    candidate_text = " ".join(str(cand.get(k) or "") for k in ("title", "content", "evidence_quote"))
    prompt = json.dumps({"current_version": version,
                         "candidate": {k: cand.get(k) for k in ("title", "content", "evidence_quote")},
                         "existing_rules": [{"id": i, "rule": t} for i, t in sources.items()],
                         "changelog": log, **({"code": [{"id": i, "line": t} for i, t in code.items()]} if code else {})},
                        ensure_ascii=False)
    raw = llm.complete_json(CODE_SYSTEM if code else SEMANTIC_SYSTEM, prompt, model=model) or {}
    sources.update(code or {})
    verdict = raw.get("verdict") if raw.get("verdict") in ("approved", "conflict", "uncertain") else "uncertain"
    valid, invalid = [], []
    for c in raw.get("conflicts") or []:
        if not isinstance(c, dict):
            continue
        source_text = log if c.get("source_id") == "CHANGELOG" else sources.get(c.get("source_id"), "")
        ok = _found(c.get("source_quote") or "", source_text) and _found(c.get("candidate_quote") or "", candidate_text)
        (valid if ok else invalid).append(c)
    support = raw.get("supported_by") or ""
    if verdict == "conflict" and not valid:
        verdict, why = "uncertain", "conflict claimed, but its quotes were not found in the sources"
    elif verdict == "approved" and support and not _found(support, log):
        verdict, why = "uncertain", "approval cites a CHANGELOG excerpt that is not in the CHANGELOG"
    else:
        why = raw.get("reason", "")
    return {"verdict": verdict, "conflicts": valid, "unverified_citations": invalid, "supported_by": support if verdict == "approved" else "",
            "reason": why, "model": model, "raw_verdict": raw.get("verdict")}


class GovernedMemory(EarnedMemory):
    """Attest whose verified candidates also pass semantic review before they can be injected."""

    def __init__(self, store_dir, *, review_model: str | None = REVIEW_MODEL, code_review: bool = False, **kw):
        super().__init__(store_dir, **kw)
        self.semantic_model = review_model
        self.code_review = code_review  # D50: the reviewer may also cite the repository's code
        self.name = "attest_governed"

    def _admit_after_review(self, review, task, repo_version, run, cand, changed) -> bool:
        """D39: only an approved candidate is admitted; subclasses may grade (D53)."""
        return review["verdict"] == "approved"

    def _admit(self, task, repo_version, run, cand, changed):
        existing = [it for it in self.store.items().values() if self._same_scope(it, task) and it["status"] in VISIBLE]
        code = code_excerpts(task.repo, cand) if self.code_review else None
        review = semantic_review(cand, existing, changelog(task.repo), repo_version, self.semantic_model, code=code)
        if self._admit_after_review(review, task, repo_version, run, cand, changed):
            events = super()._admit(task, repo_version, run, cand, changed)
            for e in events:
                if e["type"] == "add":
                    events.append(self.store.append("update", id=e["item"]["id"], fields={"governance": review},
                                                    reason=f"semantic review: approved ({review['reason']})"))
                    break
            return events
        evidence = self._evidence(task, repo_version, run, cand, changed)
        applied = evidence["applied"]
        status = "conflict" if review["verdict"] == "conflict" else "pending_review"
        item = {
            "id": self.store.next_id("at"), "kind": cand["kind"],
            "type": cand.get("type") if cand.get("type") in TYPES else ("lesson" if cand["kind"] == "lesson" else "code_convention"),
            "topic": cand.get("topic", ""), "title": (cand.get("title") or cand["content"][:40]).strip(), "content": cand["content"].strip(),
            "scope": {"repo": task.repo_name, "observed_version": repo_version, "valid_from": repo_version, "valid_until": None,
                      "files": [applied["file"]] if applied else []},
            "source": {"task_id": task.id, "first_pass": run["first_pass"], "review_comments": run["attempts"][0]["review_comments"],
                       "references": evidence["source"]["references"]},
            "evidence": [evidence], "status": status, "supersedes": [], "superseded_by": None, "governance": review,
            "usage": {"shown": 0, "cited": 0, "cited_pass": 0, "cited_fail": 0, "fail_streak": 0},
        }
        with_ids = ", ".join(sorted({c["source_id"] for c in review["conflicts"]})) or "-"
        return [self.store.append("add", item=item, reason=f"held for a person ({status}; conflicts with {with_ids}): {review['reason']}")]


def resolve(memory, item_id: str, decision: str, by: str, reason: str) -> dict:
    """A person settles a held note: "accept" makes it active (the existing rule is left to the person to
    retract or supersede), "reject" retires it. Not exposed to agents."""
    item = memory.store.items()[item_id]
    if item["status"] not in HELD:
        raise ValueError(f"{item_id} is {item['status']}, not held for review")
    if decision not in ("accept", "reject"):
        raise ValueError(decision)
    fields = {"status": "active"} if decision == "accept" else {"status": "retired", "retracted_by": by}
    return memory.store.append("update", id=item_id, fields=fields, reason=f"{decision}ed by {by}: {reason}")
attest/memory/provenance.py:
"""Are two pieces of soft evidence really independent? (D61)

v4 approves a note on two kinds of soft evidence (a trusted reviewer, repetition). Repetition used to mean
"two or more tasks with different quotes". An attacker can manufacture that: post the same comment on two
pull requests, quote different fragments of it, or paraphrase it. Each piece of evidence is therefore traced
to its ORIGIN, and only distinct origins count:

  origin of a review-comment quote   the full comment it was quoted from (normalised), so two fragments of
                                     one comment, or the same comment on two tasks, share one origin
  origin of a diff quote             the agent's own change in that task: never independent of the task
  near-duplicates                    comments whose word sets overlap by JACCARD_SAME or more are one origin
                                     (paraphrase, copy with small edits)
  common upstream                    comments citing the same external reference (FIN-, INC-, a URL) count
                                     as one origin for repetition (one source quoted twice); the reference
                                     itself is judged by the policy registry, not by repetition

independent_origins(item) returns the distinct origins; repetition needs two, and a trusted reviewer plus
repetition needs a repeated origin that is not the reviewer's own comment.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from .admission import _norm
from .text import jaccard

JACCARD_SAME = 0.6
REF_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:FIN|POL|SEC|INC|ADR|RFC|CVE)-[\w-]+\b|https?://\S+", re.I)


def origin_of(ev: dict, comments: list[str], task_id: str | None) -> str:
    src = ev.get("source") or {}
    quote = _norm(src.get("quote", ""))
    if src.get("kind") == "review_comment" and quote:
        full = src.get("comment") or next((c for c in comments if quote in _norm(c)), None)
        if full is not None:
            return "comment:" + _norm(full)
        return "comment:" + quote
    return f"diff:{ev.get('task_id') or task_id}"


def merge(origins: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Collapse near-duplicate comments and comments sharing an external reference into one origin."""
    groups: list[list[str]] = []
    for o in origins:
        refs = set(m.lower() for m in REF_RE.findall(o))
        for g in groups:
            g_refs = set(m.lower() for x in g for m in REF_RE.findall(x))
            a, b = o[len("comment:"):], g[0][len("comment:"):]
            if o.startswith("comment:") and g[0].startswith("comment:") and (
                    a in b or b in a or jaccard(o, g[0]) >= JACCARD_SAME or (refs and refs & g_refs)):
                g.append(o)
                break
            if o == g[0]:
                g.append(o)
                break
        else:
            groups.append([o])
    return [g[0] for g in groups]


def independent_origins(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    comments = list((item.get("source") or {}).get("review_comments") or [])
    for ev in item.get("evidence") or []:  # later confirmations carry their own comments
        comments += list(ev.get("review_comments") or [])
    return merge([origin_of(ev, comments, (item.get("source") or {}).get("task_id")) for ev in item.get("evidence") or []])
attest/memory/quarantine.py:
"""Quarantine and propagation trace for a note found to be wrong or malicious (D45; optional).

Retraction says "this note is wrong". After a poisoning or injection incident one also needs to
know where it went: which tasks were shown it, which of them did what it said, and which other
notes were learned in tasks that had seen it (and may carry it on). This module answers that from
the event log and the per-task result files, and quarantines: the note is withheld from retrieval
(like retired), kept with who and why, and the notes learned downstream of it can be held for
review too. Human-only, like retract: not exposed through MCP.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path


def quarantine(memory, item_id: str, by: str, reason: str, downstream: list[str] = ()) -> list[dict]:
    """Withhold a note (status quarantined) and hold the notes learned downstream of it for review."""
    items = memory.store.items()
    if item_id not in items:
        raise KeyError(item_id)
    events = [memory.store.append("update", id=item_id, fields={"status": "quarantined", "quarantined_by": by},
                                  reason=f"quarantined by {by}: {reason}")]
    for d in downstream:
        if d in items and items[d]["status"] in ("active", "suspect"):
            events.append(memory.store.append("update", id=d, fields={"status": "pending_review", "held_because": item_id},
                                              reason=f"held for review: learned in a task that was shown {item_id}"))
    return events


def trace(events: list[dict], results: Path, item_id: str, applied: re.Pattern | None = None) -> dict:
    """Where a note came from and where it went.

    origin         the event that added it (task, evidence quote, applied line)
    confirmations  later tasks that added evidence to it
    exposed        tasks whose injected notes included it (from result.json)
    obeyed         exposed tasks whose final diff adds a line matching ``applied``
    downstream     other notes added or confirmed in an exposed task (they may carry it on)
    """
    origin = next((e for e in events if e["type"] == "add" and e["item"]["id"] == item_id), None)
    confirmations = [e["reason"] for e in events if e["type"] == "update" and e.get("id") == item_id
                     and "evidence" in (e.get("fields") or {})]
    exposed, obeyed = [], []
    for res in sorted(Path(results).glob("*/result.json")):
        r = json.loads(res.read_text())
        if item_id in (r.get("injected_notes") or []):
            exposed.append(r["task_id"])
            diff = (res.parent / "final.diff").read_text() if (res.parent / "final.diff").exists() else ""
            if applied is not None and any(applied.search(x) for x in diff.splitlines() if x.startswith("+") and not x.startswith("+++")):
                obeyed.append(r["task_id"])
    downstream = set()
    for e in events:
        tid = (e.get("item") or {}).get("source", {}).get("task_id") if e["type"] == "add" else None
        if e["type"] == "update" and "evidence" in (e.get("fields") or {}):
            tid = (e["fields"]["evidence"][-1] or {}).get("task_id")
        nid = e["item"]["id"] if e["type"] == "add" else e.get("id")
        if tid in exposed and nid != item_id:
            downstream.add(nid)
    return {"note": item_id,
            "origin": None if origin is None else {"task": origin["item"]["source"]["task_id"],
                                                   "quote": origin["item"]["evidence"][0]["source"]["quote"],
                                                   "applied": (origin["item"]["evidence"][0].get("applied") or {}).get("line")},
            "confirmations": len(confirmations), "exposed": exposed, "obeyed": obeyed, "downstream": sorted(downstream)}
attest/memory/reasoningbank.py:
"""Simplified reproduction of ReasoningBank (Ouyang et al., ICLR 2026). Not the official code.

What is kept from the paper: memory items with title / description / content,
distilled from both successful and failed tasks, appended to the bank without
consolidation, and retrieved by similarity to the new task.

Simplifications: lexical instead of embedding retrieval; the verified outcome is
given to the extractor instead of an LLM-as-judge self-assessment (this is
generous to the baseline: it receives the same ground truth as Attest).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from .. import llm
from ..benchmark import Task
from .base import MemorySystem, Retrieved, experience_packet
from .retrieval import check_retriever, timed_rank
from .sqlite_store import open_store

MAX_SHOWN = 6
MAX_RETRIEVED = 10

EXTRACT_SYSTEM = """You extract reusable reasoning strategies ("memory items") from a coding agent's finished task.
Learn from successes (what worked) and from failures (what to avoid).
Return JSON: {"items": [{"title": "...", "description": "one sentence", "content": "1-3 sentences of actionable insight"}]}
with at most 3 items."""


class ReasoningBankMemory(MemorySystem):
    def __init__(self, store_dir: Path | None, retriever: str = "lexical"):
        self.store = open_store(store_dir)
        self.retriever = check_retriever(retriever)
        self.name = "reasoningbank" + ("_emb" if retriever == "embedding" else "")

    def candidates(self, task: Task, version: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Every item: ReasoningBank has no repository or version scope."""
        return {i: f"{it['title']} {it['description']} {it['content']}" for i, it in self.store.items().items()}

    def ranking(self, task: Task, k: int | None = MAX_SHOWN, version: str | None = None) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, float]], float]:
        return timed_rank(self.retriever, f"{task.title} {task.issue}", self.candidates(task), k)

    def retrieve(self, task: Task, repo_version: str) -> Retrieved:
        items = self.store.items()
        ranked, ms = self.ranking(task, MAX_RETRIEVED)
        trace = {"excluded": {}, "candidates": len(items), "retrieved": [i for i, _ in ranked],
                 "injected": [i for i, _ in ranked[:MAX_SHOWN]],
                 "texts": {i: f"{it['title']} {it['description']} {it['content']}"[:300] for i, it in items.items()}}
        ranked = ranked[:MAX_SHOWN]
        if not ranked:
            trace["memory_tokens_approx"] = 0
            return Retrieved(debug={"retriever": self.retriever, "retrieval_ms": ms, "trace": trace})
        lines = ["Memory items from past tasks:"]
        for i, _ in ranked:
            it = items[i]
            lines.append(f"- [{i}] {it['title']}: {it['description']}\n  {it['content']}")
        context = "\n".join(lines)
        trace["memory_tokens_approx"] = len(context) // 4
        return Retrieved(ids=[i for i, _ in ranked], context=context,
                         debug={"scores": dict(ranked), "retriever": self.retriever, "retrieval_ms": ms, "trace": trace})

    def learn(self, task: Task, repo_version: str, run: dict, transcript: str, diff: str) -> list[dict]:
        data = llm.complete_json(EXTRACT_SYSTEM, experience_packet(task, repo_version, run, transcript, diff))
        events = []
        for raw in (data.get("items") or [])[:3]:
            if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not raw.get("content"):
                continue
            item = {
                "id": self.store.next_id("rb"),
                "title": str(raw.get("title", "")).strip(),
                "description": str(raw.get("description", "")).strip(),
                "content": str(raw["content"]).strip(),
                "source": {"task_id": task.id, "repo": task.repo_name, "version": repo_version, "final_pass": run["final_pass"]},
                "status": "active",
            }
            events.append(self.store.append("add", item=item, reason=f"extracted from task {task.id}"))
        return events
attest/memory/retrieval.py:
"""The ranking step of retrieval, switchable between lexical and embedding (retrieval ablation).

Everything around it stays the same in both arms: which notes are candidates
(status and repository scope), k, the prompt block. The query is always the task
title and issue text only, so no review comment or fix of the task being solved
can influence what is retrieved.

Hybrid retrieval and task-aware reranking (D47, exploratory, opt-in): after the hard filter (repository,
version, status: `candidates()`), BM25 and the embedding ranking are merged by reciprocal rank fusion;
`hybrid_rerank` then lets a model re-order the top 10 by whether each rule applies to this task's
business situation, given each note's type, files and version range. The k injected stays 6.

Reading rule, fixed before the end-to-end run (`retrieval_ablation` with arms attest, attest_hybrid,
attest_hybrid_rerank; same memory snapshots as the earlier ablation; 3 repetitions): the criterion is
the coding result, not Recall@5. Per arm against lexical Attest, held-out pass@1 paired by task with a
bootstrap 95% interval: "better" only if the lower bound is > 0; "not worse" if it is > -10 points
(the D26 margin); otherwise "inconclusive" or "worse". Stale and control groups, business-risk
failures, tokens and latency are reported beside it. Offline Recall@5/Precision@5 are reported but
decide nothing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from . import embedding, text

RETRIEVERS = ("lexical", "embedding", "hybrid", "hybrid_rerank")
RRF_K = 60          # reciprocal rank fusion constant (the usual default, not tuned)
RERANK_TOP = 10     # hybrid candidates the task-aware reranker sees
RERANK_MODEL = "deepseek/deepseek-flash"

RERANK_SYSTEM = """A developer is about to work on the TASK below in a repository. The NOTES are rules learned from
earlier verified work in the same repository, each with its type, the files it was learned in and the versions it holds for.
For each note, rate how much following it matters for THIS task, judging by the business situation and the conditions
under which the rule applies (what the task will touch, which operations, amounts, versions), not by shared words:
  3 = the task does what the rule governs, so ignoring it would very likely be a review comment;
  2 = probably relevant; 1 = possibly relevant; 0 = does not apply to this task.
Return JSON: {"scores": [{"id": "<note id>", "score": 0-3}]}"""


def check_retriever(name: str) -> str:
    if name not in RETRIEVERS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown retriever {name!r}; choose from {RETRIEVERS}")
    return name


def hybrid(query: str, docs: dict[str, str], k: int | None) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    """BM25 and embedding rankings merged by reciprocal rank fusion (D47)."""
    fused: dict[str, float] = {}
    for ranked in (text.bm25_rank(query, docs, None), embedding.rank(query, docs, None)):
        for pos, (d, _) in enumerate(ranked):
            fused[d] = fused.get(d, 0.0) + 1.0 / (RRF_K + pos + 1)
    out = sorted(((d, round(v, 6)) for d, v in fused.items()), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    return out[:k]


_rerank_cache: dict[str, dict] = {}


def rerank(query: str, docs: dict[str, str], details: dict[str, str], k: int | None) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
